p0.original: 第四章 体会和表达感受
p0.en: Chapter IV. Understanding and expression of feelings

p1.original: 非暴力沟通的第二个要素是感受。心理学家罗洛·梅（Rollo May）认为：“成熟的人十分敏锐，就像听交响乐的不同乐章，不论是热情奔放，还是柔和舒缓，他都能体察到细微的起伏。”然而，根据罗洛·梅的叙述，大多数人的感受“像军号声那样单调”。
p1.en: The second element of Nonviolent Communication is feeling. According to a psychologist, Rollo May, “The mature are keen, like the different instruments of the symphony, whether it be warm or soft, that he can see the slight rise and fall. However, according to Rolo May, most people feel “singlely like the sound of the military.

p3.original: 我在美国学校学了21年，却想不起有什么人问过我的感受。人们认为感受是无关紧要的，重要的是各种权威主张的“正确思想”。于是，我们被鼓励服从权威而非倾听自己。渐渐地，我们习惯于考虑：“人们期待我怎么做？”
p3.en: I've been in American schools for 21 years, but I can't think of anyone asking me how I feel. The perception was considered irrelevant, but what was important was the “right mind” of the various authoritative claims. We are therefore encouraged to obey authority rather than to listen to ourselves. Gradually, we're used to thinking, "What do people expect me to do?

p4.original: 9岁那年，有一天放学后，几个男孩在校外等着打我。我躲在教室不敢回家。老师发现后，叫我离开学校。我说我很害怕，她教训说：“男孩子不要胆小怕事。”几年后，作为运动员，我的感受更显得微不足道。教练们特别看重运动员“全力以赴”的精神——即使身体经受着剧痛，也要继续比赛。有一次，我的手腕骨折了，没有接受任何治疗，忍痛打了一个月的棒球。
p4.en: At the age of 9, one day after school, several boys were waiting outside school to hit me. I'm hiding in the classroom and I'm afraid to go home. When the teacher found out, he told me to leave school. I said I was scared, and she taught me, "Boys don't be afraid of things. A few years later, as an athlete, my feelings became even more insignificant. In particular, the coaches value the spirit of the athletes “with all their energy” — to continue the race even if they experience severe physical pain. On one occasion, my wrist was broken, without any medical treatment and a month of hard baseball.

p5.original: 在一次研讨班中，一位大学生说，室友将音响的声音放得很大，他怎么也睡不着。我询问他当时的感受，他说：“我觉得在晚上不该这么大声。”我提醒他，虽然他用“觉得”这个词，但他表达的是看法而非感受。我请他再试着表达感受，这一次，他说：“声音太大了就会打扰到别人。”我向他解释，这依然是看法而非感受。他想了想，斩钉截铁地说：“我没什么感受！”
p5.en: At one of the seminars, a university student said that his roommate was able to sleep when he played the sound loud. I asked him how he felt, and he said, "I don't think it's supposed to be so loud at night. I remind him that, although he uses the word “like”, he expresses views rather than feelings. I asked him to try to express his feelings again, and this time he said, "If the sound is too loud, it bothers others. I explained to him that it was still a view, not a feeling. And he thought, "I don't feel anything!

p6.original: 很明显，他有强烈的感受。不幸的是，他体会不到，更不用说表达它们了。体会和表达感受并不容易。根据我的观察，对于从事律师、工程师、警察、经理等职业的人来说，尤为困难——表达感受与他们的职业形象相冲突。在家庭中，如果家庭成员无法表达情感，那是很悲哀的。西部乡村音乐的代表人物瑞芭·麦克英特尔在她父亲去世后写了一首歌：《我所不知道的最伟大的人》，这首歌引起许多人的共鸣——他们渴望与父亲沟通情感，却又做不到。
p6.en: Apparently, he had a strong feeling. Unfortunately, he could not feel, let alone express them. It is not easy to feel and express feelings. According to my observations, it is particularly difficult for people who work as lawyers, engineers, police officers, managers, etc. — expressing feelings that conflict with their professional image. In the family, it is sad if family members are unable to express their feelings. The representative of Western Country Music, Reba McInter, wrote a song after her father's death: "The Greatest Man I Don't Know," which resonates with many people who desire to communicate with their father but fail to do so.

p7.original: 我常听到这样的声明：“我不想误导你，我的男人真的很棒，但我从不了解他的感受。”有一次，一对夫妻一起参加了一个研讨班，期间，太太对先生说：“我觉得我嫁给了一堵墙。”先生的反应真的就像一堵墙：他坐在那里一动不动。太太气坏了，转向我，嚷道：“看！他总是这样。坐在一边，闷声不响。和他过日子，就像对着一堵墙。”
p7.en: I've heard this often: “I don't want to mislead you, my man is really good, but I never understood his feelings. One time, a couple attended a seminar, during which the wife said to the gentleman: "I think I'm married to a wall. "Mr.'s reaction is really like a wall: he sits there and he doesn't move. The wife was so angry, turned to me, and said, "Look! He always does. Sit on one side, squirt. Living with him is like facing a wall.

p8.original: “你是不是感到孤单，希望先生多体贴你呢？”我问道。在她表示认同后，我试图说明，“我觉得我嫁给了一堵墙”这种话很难提醒她先生留意她的愿望。一旦认为自己受到了指责，他很可能就会觉得委屈并退缩，这样，双方的关系甚至会更加疏远。例如，如果他感到伤心、沮丧，不作任何反应，在妻子的心目中，他就会真的像一堵墙。
p8.en: "Do you feel lonely and wish Mr. Be kind to you? I asked. After expressing her agreement, I tried to explain that the phrase “I feel I have married a wall” was difficult to remind her husband of her wishes. Once he felt accused, he was likely to feel frustrated and retreated, so that the relationship between the two sides could become even more alienated. For example, if he was sad, frustrated and did not react, he would really look like a wall in his wife's eyes.

p9.original: 表达内心的感受，不仅可以促进亲情，还可以改善工作。有一次，瑞士一家大公司的技术部门找到了我。他们面临的难题是，其他部门的人不愿和他们打交道。其他部门的职员在接受调查时说：“我们不喜欢请教他们。那就像和一堆机器说话。”了解到这个情况后，我鼓励技术部门的职员更经常地表达感受。后来，情况有了好转。
p9.en: The expression of inner feelings not only promotes affection but also improves work. One time, the technical department of a large Swiss company found me. The challenge for them is that people in other sectors are reluctant to deal with them. The staff of the other departments said in the survey: “We don't like to ask them. That's like talking to a bunch of machines. I have learned that, and I encourage technical staff to express their feelings more often. The situation has since improved.

p10.original: 另有一次，我应邀去协助一所医院的管理层。他们有一个项目需要医生的支持。可是，不久前，医生们以17∶1否决了那个项目。为了争取支持，他们准备再次举行医生会议。他们期待非暴力沟通能够促进他们与医生的沟通。
p10.en: On another occasion, I was invited to assist the management of a hospital. They have a project that needs the support of doctors. However, not long ago, the doctors rejected the project by 17:1. In order to gain support, they are prepared to hold another meeting of doctors. They expect Nonviolent Communication to facilitate their communication with doctors.

p11.original: 在模拟管理层与医生的对话时，我扮演的是管理人员的角色。我一开始就说：“再一次提到这个项目，我忐忑不安。”选择这样的开场白，是因为我注意到，管理层极为担心再次受挫。我还没来得及往下说，一位负责人就打断了我，“你太不现实了！我们决不能告诉医生我们感到不安。”
p11.en: I played the role of manager in simulated management-doctor dialogue. I said at the beginning: “I am troubled to mention this item again. This introductory statement was chosen because I noted that management was extremely concerned about the setback again. I couldn't get down to it, and one of the people in charge interrupted me, "You're so unrealistic! We must not tell the doctors that we are disturbed.

p12.original: 于是，我就问他，为什么这是绝不可能的事情。他脱口而出：“一旦我们示弱，他们就会更加盛气凌人。”对他的回答，我并不意外。毕竟，对于许多人来说，在工作时表达情感是无法想象的事情。然而，有位负责人还是决定试一试。这次，他不像平时那样面无表情地陈述观点——他不仅解释了医生改变立场的重要意义，而且还表达了内心的感受。医生的反应十分不同。他们非但没有“盛气凌人”，而且还以17∶1通过了项目。这个戏剧性的转变提醒管理层，工作中示弱也有助于解决问题。
p12.en: So I asked him why that was impossible. And he said, "When we are weak, they will be even more aggressive. I'm not surprised by the answer to him. After all, it is inconceivable for many to express feelings at work. However, one of the leaders decided to try. This time, he did not express his views without face — he explained not only the importance of the doctor's changing position, but also the feelings he felt inside. The doctor's response was very different. Instead of being “smuggling”, they adopted the project at 17:1. This dramatic shift reminds management that weakness in work also helps to solve problems.

p13.original: 还有一次，我去给一些学生讲解非暴力沟通。第一天，我一走进教室，学生就安静下来，不再热烈交谈。我说：“早上好！”可是，一片沉默。我很不自在，但不好意思说出来。接着，我若无其事地开始上课：“本节课，我们将学习一种沟通模式。我希望，它能促进你们的家庭关系和友谊。”
p13.en: And again, I went to talk to some students about Nonviolent Communication. On the first day, as soon as I walked into the classroom, the students quieted down and stopped talking. I said, "Good morning! But, it's silent. I'm uncomfortable, but I'm embarrassed to say it. And then I started without a thing: "This class, we'll learn a mode of communication. I hope that it will promote your family relations and friendship. I'm sorry.

p14.original: 我接着继续介绍非暴力沟通，但看起来没有人在听。有个女孩翻着包，从中掏出一把指甲锉，开始使劲修指甲。靠窗的学生把脸贴在玻璃上，仿佛街上发生了令人振奋的事情。我越发觉得不自在，但还是什么也没说。终于，有个学生突然插话——他显然比我更勇敢：“你讨厌黑人，不是吗？”我愣了一下，但马上意识到，我试图隐藏自己的不安促成了这种印象。
p14.en: I went on to introduce Nonviolent Communication, but nobody seemed to be listening. A girl flipped over and pulled a nail out of it and started working hard on her nails. The window students put their faces on the glass as if something exciting had happened on the street. I feel uncomfortable, but I haven't said anything. Finally, a student suddenly intervened -- he was obviously braver than I was: "You hate black people, don't you? “I paused, but immediately realized that I tried to hide my unease and contributed to that impression.

p15.original: “我很紧张，”我坦白地说，“但不是因为你的肤色。而是因为我和大家是初次见面，我希望得到肯定。”示弱产生了积极影响。他们开始了解我、介绍他们自己，并询问有关非暴力沟通的问题。
p15.en: "I'm nervous," I said, frankly, "but not because of your skin colour. It's because I'm meeting with you for the first time, and I want to be sure. Weaknesses have had a positive impact. They began to know me, introduce themselves and ask questions about Nonviolent Communication.

p17.original: 在非暴力沟通中，我们注意区分感受和想法。
p17.en: In Nonviolent Communication, we pay attention to distinguishing between feelings and ideas.

p19.en: I don't think I play the guitar well.

p20.original: 在这个句子中，我评价自己吉他弹得好不好，而没有表达感受。
p20.en: In this sentence, I judge myself as good as it is, without expressing my feelings.

p22.en: • As a guitarist, I'm a little lost.

p25.original: 如果认为自己吉他弹得不好，我可能会失落、郁闷或厌烦。
p25.en: I may be lost, depressed or bored if I think I play my guitar badly.

p26.original: 当我们说“我觉得”，我们常常并不是在表达感受，而是在表达想法。例如，有时我们会说：“我觉得这不公平。”在这句话中，“我觉得”换成“我认为”也许更恰当。以下是更多的例句：
p26.en: When we say “I think” we are often expressing our feelings not, but our thoughts. For example, sometimes we say, "I don't think it's fair. In this sentence, I think it might be more appropriate to replace the words “I think” with “I think”. The following are more examples:

p27.en: - I think you should know more.

p29.en: - I think the boss is mean.

p31.original: 还有些词表达的是想法，而非感受。例如：被抛弃、被羞辱、被虐待、被打扰、被拒绝、不受重视、被束缚、被欺负、无人理睬、得不到支持、无人赏识、被利用、被贬低。
p31.en: There are also words that express ideas, not feelings. For example, being abandoned, humiliated, abused, disturbed, rejected, unimportant, restrained, bullied, ignored, unsupported, unappreciated, unappreciated, exploited and demeaned.

p34.original: “被误解”一词反映了我认为别人不理解我。此时，我可能会很着急。
p34.en: The word “misunderstanding” reflects what I think is not understood. I might be in a hurry.

p36.original: “被忽略”是我们的判断。此时，如果想独处，我们就会很高兴；反之，如果想参加活动，就会感到难过。
p36.en: “neglected” is our judgement. At this point, we'd be happy to be alone; On the contrary, it would be sad to want to participate.

p37.original: 建立表达感受的词汇表
p37.en: Create vocabulary for expression of feelings

p38.original: 清楚地表达感受需要丰富的词汇。“很好”或“很差”这样的词语很难让人明白我们实际的状况。例如，如果我们说“我感觉良好”，“良好”这个词所表达的感受可能是高兴、轻松、欣慰或别的。为了更好地沟通情感，非暴力沟通主张使用具体的语言。
p38.en: Clear expression of feelings requires rich vocabulary. The words “good” or “very bad” are hard to understand. For example, if we say “I feel good”, the word “good” may express feelings of pleasure, ease, comfort or something. In order to better communicate feelings, Nonviolent Communication advocates the use of specific languages.

p39.original: 为了清晰地表达感受，我们编制了以下的词汇表。
p39.en: In order to give a clear expression to the feeling, we have prepared the following glossary.

p40.original: （1）下列词语可用来表达我们的需要得到满足时的感受：
p40.en: (1) The following terms may be used to express the feelings of our needs when they are met:

p41.original: 兴奋 喜悦 欣喜 甜蜜 精力充沛 兴高采烈
p41.en: Excited, joyful, joyful, sweet, energetic, high.

p42.original: 感激 感动 乐观 自信 振作 振奋 开心
p42.en: Thank you, moved, optimistic, confident, cheer up, cheer up, happy.

p43.original: 高兴 快乐 愉快 幸福 陶醉 满足 欣慰 心旷神怡
p43.en: # Happy, happy, happy, intoxicated, satisfied, comforted, unattractive #

p45.original: 平静 自在 舒适 放松 踏实 安全 温暖 放心 无忧无虑
p45.en: Calm, comfortable, relaxed, firm, safe, warm, safe and secure.

p46.original: （2）下列词语可用来表达我们的需要没有得到满足时的感受：
p46.en: (2) The following terms may be used to express the feeling that our needs are not met:

p47.original: 害怕 担心 焦虑 忧虑 着急 紧张 心神不宁 心烦意乱
p47.en: Fear, fear, anxiety, anxiety, anxiety, stress, unease, discomfort.

p48.original: 忧伤 沮丧 灰心 气馁 泄气 绝望 伤感 凄凉 悲伤
p48.en: Sadness, depression, frustration, depression, despair, despair, sadness, desolation, sadness.

p49.original: 恼怒 愤怒 烦恼 苦恼 生气 厌烦 不满 不快 不耐烦
p49.en: Angry, anger, distress, anguish, anger, discomfort, displeasure, impatience, impatience.

p51.original: 震惊 失望 困惑 茫然 寂寞 孤独 郁闷 难过 悲观
p51.en: Astonishment, disappointment, confusion, confusion, loneliness, loneliness, depression, sadness, pessimism

p52.original: 沉重 麻木 精疲力尽 委靡不振 疲惫不堪 昏昏欲睡
p52.en: Heavy, numb, exhausted, insolent, exhausted, sleepy.

p53.en: I don't know what to say.

p54.original: 尴尬 惭愧 内疚 妒忌 遗憾 不舒服
p54.en: I'm embarrassed, ashamed, guilty, jealous, sorry, uncomfortable.

p56.original: 非暴力沟通的第二个要素是感受。通过建立表达感受的词汇表，我们可以更清楚地表达感受，从而使沟通更为顺畅。在表达感受时，示弱有助于解决冲突。此外，非暴力沟通还对表达具体感受的词语与陈述想法、评论以及观点的词语作了区分。
p56.en: The second element of Nonviolent Communication is feeling. By creating a vocabulary for expression of feelings, we can express them more clearly, thus making communication smoother. In expressing feelings, signs of weakness help to resolve conflicts. In addition, Nonviolent Communication distinguishes between words that express specific feelings and those that present ideas, comments and views.

p58.original: 看看以下的句子是否表达了感受。请标出那些表达感受的句子。
p58.en: Let's see if the following sentences express feelings. Please mark out those sentences that express feelings.

p60.en: “I am so sorry that you are leaving.

p61.original: 3.“当你说那句话时，我感到害怕。”
p61.en: “When you say that, I feel afraid.

p62.original: 4.“如果你不和我打招呼，我会觉得你不在乎我。”
p62.en: “If you don't say hello to me, I think you don't care about me.

p63.en: “I am pleased to have you here.

p64.en: “You are such a pain in the ass.

p66.en: “I feel that I have been misunderstood.

p67.en: “I am happy that you have helped me.

p69.original: 以下是我对练习二的理解：
p69.en: Here's my understanding of practice two:

p70.original: 1.如果你认为这一句是感受，我们意见不一致。我不认为“你不爱我”是感受。对我来说，它是对他人生活感受的判断。以下例句表达了感受：“我很伤心”或“我十分痛苦”。
p70.en: 1. If you think this sentence is a feeling, we are not in agreement. I don't think "you don't love me" is a feeling. For me, it's a judgement about how people feel about their lives. The following example expresses the feeling: “I am sad” or “I am very painful”.

p71.original: 2.如果你认为这一句是感受，我们意见一致。
p71.en: 2. If you think this sentence is a feeling, we agree.

p72.original: 3.如果你认为这一句是感受，我们意见一致。
p72.en: 3. If you think this sentence is a feeling, we agree.

p73.original: 4.如果你认为这一句是感受，我们意见不一致。我不认为“你不在乎我”是感受。对我来说，它是对他人态度的判断。以下例句表达了感受：“我进来的时候，你没和我打招呼，我感到孤单。”
p73.en: 4. If you think this sentence is a feeling, we are not in agreement. I don't think "you don't care about me" is a feeling. For me, it is a judgment of the attitude of others. The following example: “When I came in, you didn't say hello to me, I felt alone.

p74.original: 5.如果你认为这一句是感受，我们意见一致。
p74.en: 5. If you think this sentence is a feeling, we agree.

p75.original: 6.如果你认为这一句是感受，我们意见不一致。我不认为“可恶”是感受。对我来说，它是评价。以下例句表达了感受：“我有些烦躁。”
p75.en: 6. If you think this sentence is a feeling, we are not in agreement. I don't think "damn" is a feeling. For me, it's evaluation. The following example shows how it feels: "I'm a little upset.

p76.original: 7.如果你认为这一句是感受，我们意见不一致。我不认为“想打你”是感受。对我来说，它表达的是想法。以下例句表达了感受：“想到你，我就火冒三丈。”
p76.en: If you think this sentence is a feeling, we are not in agreement. I don't think "want to hit you" is a feeling. For me, it's an idea. And the following example is: "I think of you, and I'm angry.

p77.original: 8.如果你认为这一句是感受，我们意见不一致。我不认为“被人误解”是感受。对我来说，它是对他人观点的判断。以下例句表达了感受：“我感到郁闷”或“我很灰心”。
p77.en: If you think this sentence is a feeling, we are not in agreement. I don't think it's "misunderstanding" to feel. For me, it is a judgement of the views of others. The following example expresses the feeling: “I am depressed” or “I am frustrated”.

p78.original: 9.如果你认为这一句是感受，我们意见一致。然而，“开心”这个词含义较为模糊。我们可以借助其他词语更清楚地表达自己。在这个例子中，发言者的感受可能是：“欣慰”、“满足”或“鼓舞”。
p78.en: 9. If you think this sentence is a feeling, we agree. However, the word “happiness” is vague. We can express ourselves more clearly by other words. In this example, the speaker's feeling might be “comfort”, “satisfaction” or “encourage”.

p79.original: 10.如果你认为这一句是感受，我们意见不一致。我不认为“没用的人”是感受。对我来说，它是发言者的自我评价。以下例句表达了感受：“我很沮丧”或“我十分伤心”。
p79.en: 10. If you consider this sentence to be a feeling, we are not in agreement. I don't think "no use" is a feeling. For me, it is a self-evaluation of speakers. The following example expresses the feeling: “I am depressed” or “I am very sad”.
